source_identity_note: W23S006 is a complete single 73-page lecture-notes contribution published as a chapter in Clay Mathematics Proceedings 15 (pp.395–467), not a complete reading of that volume. It is counted once as a paper/proceedings contribution; no whole-monograph read is claimed.
canonical_reuse_credit_basis: The original W08 reads were accepted in R05; W23 usage cards were accepted separately by R03. W23 does not claim either as a new full-text read.

legacy_mother_status_snapshot.resolution: The old status file is preserved byte-for-byte. Its 19 accepted/11 pending values describe the pre-final-mother-binding snapshot. The final R03 mother decision later passed all 30 source bindings, preserving the previous 28 and adding S029–S030. This is a status transition, not a change to the mother ledger.

open_interfaces: C107: no proof of tightness for the fixed-lattice SAW curve, discrete domain-Markov/conditioning interface, curve-topology convergence, or SLE(8/3) identification.

C108: Lacoin proves a deterministic root-independent limsup rate and a strict planar quenched/annealed gap; the almost-sure full nth-root limit and root independence for that limit remain unproved/conjectural in the cited source.

evidence_classes.proof: Only source theorems with matching model/hypotheses and verified proof dependencies.
evidence_classes.conditional_method: Reusable template explicitly conditioned on all source hypotheses and outstanding interfaces.
evidence_classes.numerical: Actual local MATLAB/Python outputs are finite algebra/count checks only, never asymptotic proof.

integrity: integrity_manifest.json; SHA-256 for each packaged file except the manifest itself, whose digest is integrity_manifest.sha256.
counting_note: The 27 articles/preprints comprise 25 full-text paper-kind research papers plus two preprints; S006 is the 26th paper-kind full-text record but is reported separately as one complete proceedings-chapter contribution. Two additional paper-kind SLE works are canonical usages, not new reads. Thus 28 full-text reads + 2 canonical uses = 30 distinct accepted works.
